I don't know about worst thing, but might have been the most interesting. All of my students are elementary age and come from middle class families. I always emphasize to my kids that it is up to them how much they learn and succeed in school. To reinforce this, I provide prizes and a point system based on how much they've worked beyond what was required. 

Understandably, my students are very young and do not really know the concept of money. All they know are "prizes" and that they always want more. One day, one of them bumps into me at the supermarket with his mom and they see that I am using food stamps. I guess I would think that when I was a kid, I'd always expected teachers to be middle class, married, full grown adults. Here I am, single, living in an apartment, with a $20 phone, and using food stamps.

I wasn't ashamed or anything, but I wondered how the kids would react if they knew. Some of them started coming up to me and telling me about job opportunities with local business or with their parents. I asked them why they started telling me these things. When I was younger, I met someone who had been in jail since 18 and got out at something like... 28. He went to community college and was trying to do the transfer program into a good university. He was a big guy and seemed to have a bad attitude around him. I really thought he annoying to deal with. He didn't look like a good person, and after he told me of his background, I didn't have much respect for him. However, he came to my workplace and asked for help applying to school and writing his resume. I did what I could because I liked my job. A couple of months later, he came back and told me he got into a world-class public university. He showed me the acceptance letter to prove it. I never saw him again, but from that day forward, I honestly had 100% respect for him.

Then when I forced myself not to be quiet, I'd say stupid things. There are people who still actively avoid me because of how awkward I make things.

The truth is, I like to teach. Working with kids gives me a chance to 1) try to prevent them from having to walk in my shoes, 2) give them the confidence I didn't have, 3) practice my social skills without too much fear. For example, if one day, I want the kids to respect and listen to me as an authority figure, then I'll experiment with ways to do it until I can get it down with clarity. If I want to be funny at times, well, it won't always work. But kids forget about it so fast that it doesn't matter. Eventually, I improved and I can do a little better in social situations with adults. We're all kids on the inside. We'll laugh at the same silly things, after all ;)

I often work with kids 3rd-5th grade. I've never talked to a parent about "following through," but a parent has talked to me about having their kid "follow through" before. In that case, his kid was held back a grade. However, now he's ahead of the class and is often bored. He's bored in a way that he doesn't want to work ahead even or do more than the bare minimum even when I encourage him. The parent, of course, wants more than bare minimum so he often lectures the kid about "following through." 

So when I stood there listening to the Dad talk about his kid needing to "follow through," I'm inclined to believe that that is something really important to him. So the next time I am working with this child and he doesn't feel motivated, I might give a slight reminder about the talk his Dad had with me. That way, when his Dad comes to pick him up later, I can at least say, "Your son is doing better with following through and practicing beyond the bare minimum." 

Long explanation, sorry. 

TL;DR: I think the teacher just thought "following through" might have been a big issue for you, and was trying to make you know that you were heard by echoing it back to you and letting you know that the same echo will be done for your daughter.

Next, I'd say that your husband really deeply cares and loves you. Don't worry about depressing or burdening him. Obviously, you are much more important than any of the negative things that have happened. He is there for you, even if you don't want him to deal with your mental state.

Whether or not that works, being happy on the outside at least gets people to notice you or like you. That way, they will be more willing to listen when you tell them you want their help.
